title: PPFD, Photoperiod and Repeatable Canopy Light Checks

content.overview: Lighting measurements are meaningful only when the measurement method represents the crop. Learners practice distinguishing fixture settings from canopy measurements, recording photoperiod and PPFD with correct context, using repeatable canopy grids, and recognizing why one bright center reading or a changed meter angle cannot describe whole-canopy light distribution.

vocabulary.definition: Photosynthetic photon flux density: the flux of photosynthetically active photons reaching a surface per unit area and time.
The scheduled duration and timing of the light and dark periods.
A repeatable set of canopy positions used to characterize spatial light distribution.
The degree to which measured light intensity is distributed consistently across a defined canopy area.

sections.title: Fixture output is not the same as canopy PPFD
sections.body: A fixture setting, rated output or dimmer percentage does not tell a technician exactly how much photosynthetically active light reaches every canopy location. PPFD is measured at the crop plane, and canopy geometry, fixture layout, distance and surrounding surfaces can change distribution.

sections.title: One point cannot describe spatial distribution
sections.body: A center reading can be useful for that point but may hide brighter or dimmer regions elsewhere. A repeatable measurement grid keeps height, orientation and positions consistent so maps can be compared over time or after authorized changes.

sections.title: Photoperiod records preserve schedule and observation
sections.body: Technicians may verify timer or controller schedules and observe lights-on/lights-off states within their procedure. A record should distinguish the intended schedule from what was actually observed, including any discrepancy or alarm, without independently changing crop strategy unless authorized.

workedExamples: A nine-point canopy grid has an acceptable average but a much brighter center and dimmer corners. The technician records the distribution instead of reporting only the average.
After an authorized fixture-height change, the same measurement grid, height and meter orientation are repeated so the before/after maps are comparable.
commonMistakes: Using only the brightest center measurement as the room PPFD.
Changing measurement height or sensor orientation between maps.
Treating a fixture dimmer percentage as a direct canopy PPFD value.
Changing photoperiod because a schedule discrepancy is observed without checking the supplied authority/process.
content.practicalApplication: Use the downloadable PPFD and sensor-verification practice sheet with a supplied room map and readings. Preserve the measurement grid, height/orientation, each point, units and time; summarize distribution without hiding extremes; record intended versus observed photoperiod; and document any outlier verification or escalation required by the scenario.
content.summary: Technician I light work focuses on repeatable measurement and accurate records. PPFD should be tied to canopy location and method, spatial distribution should not be hidden by one point or average, and photoperiod discrepancies are documented and escalated within authorization.

items.title: Define the grid
items.body: Use the supplied or approved canopy positions.

items.title: Hold the measurement plane
items.body: Keep sensor height and orientation consistent with the defined method.

items.title: Record each point
items.body: Preserve PPFD value, units, position and time.

items.title: Summarize distribution
items.body: Report average/range or other required uniformity information without hiding extreme points.

items.title: Escalate discrepancies
items.body: Route unexpected distribution or photoperiod states through the supplied procedure rather than independently redesigning the lighting strategy.

blocks.title: Repeatable canopy PPFD grid
blocks.alt: Nine-point canopy PPFD map with a brighter center and dimmer edges, plus reminders to keep measurement height, sensor orientation and grid positions consistent and to report every point with units and context.
blocks.caption: A repeatable grid preserves spatial light distribution; one bright center point, fixture setting or average cannot replace the canopy map.

blocks.title: Downloadable practice: PPFD grid and sensor verification
blocks.body: Use this printable worksheet to record a nine-point PPFD grid with consistent measurement method, summarize distribution without hiding extremes, compare intended and observed photoperiod, and practice structured sensor-outlier verification within the Technician I authority boundary.
blocks.label: Open PPFD and sensor-verification practice sheet

blocks.title: Bright center reading
blocks.setting: The center canopy point is 950 while several edge points are near 500. The facility asks for a room light check.
options: Room PPFD is 950 because the center is most important
Report the full repeatable grid and its distribution rather than substituting the center point for the canopy
Move the meter closer to the fixture until all points match
Delete edge readings because they lower the average
blocks.answer: Report the full repeatable grid and its distribution rather than substituting the center point for the canopy
blocks.feedback: Spatial mapping is specifically intended to reveal distribution that one point cannot represent.
